topic: Relations and their Domains and Ranges
title: Only the True Pairs! Relations Explained Simply | PUC Maths Class 11
description:
Five classmates and four blood groups make twenty possible pairs, but only a few are true. How do we keep just the true pairs, and describe them in maths? In this animated lesson for PUC and Class 11 Maths (NCERT Chapter 2, Relations and Functions) we meet relations and their domain, range and codomain.

You will watch all twenty pairs of a Cartesian product tested live while the false ones fade, leaving a relation. Then the NCERT definition, the image of an element, the domain, range and codomain lit up on an arrow diagram, range versus codomain side by side with a pause-and-think, a step-by-step proof that there are 2 to the power pq relations with four live switches running through all sixteen, a worked example, the exam trap in counting relations, an original JEE Main pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11 and JEE Main students.

In this video:
0:00 20 possible pairs, only 4 true
0:29 Live: test every pair of S × G
0:55 Definition: a relation is a subset of A × B
1:18 Domain, range and codomain
1:46 Range vs codomain: side by side
2:00 Pause and think: a new arrow
2:28 How many relations? 2 to the power pq
3:06 Worked example: y = 2x on A
3:52 Exam trap: counting relations
4:10 Where it is asked
4:21 Practice question (JEE Main pattern)
5:08 Recap and three questions to answer

Next episode (Ep 16): Functions as Mappings. Every roll number points to exactly one student. When every element gets exactly one arrow, a relation becomes a function.

Video by Quest Academy.
